title: Integration tests: staged rollouts for Dedicated pools (gate failures + rollback)
author: Leila Farouk
release_notes: Internal: adds end-to-end integration coverage for Dedicated staged rollouts (plan creation, promotion, gate fail, auto-abort/rollback, and idempotent retries).
body: Summary: This PR adds end-to-end integration tests for the Dedicated staged rollouts path using a simulated Dedicated pool + fake telemetry backend. The goal is to validate that control-plane state transitions, routing partition selection, stage-tagged telemetry, gate evaluation semantics, and rollback behavior work together (and stay working as we iterate). Context: We’ve had early beta regressions where canary partitions effectively reduced capacity and triggered 429s (SUP-28522) and where gate evidence panels were empty due to telemetry tag mismatch (SUP-28605). These tests are intended to catch those classes of failures before changes land in main. What’s included: (1) Happy path rollout: create DedicatedPoolRolloutPlan -> start running -> promote through stages -> complete, with assertions on audit events and deterministic stage selection. (2) Gate failure scenario: simulate elevated 5xx + p99 latency in stage=canary and confirm policy engine returns FAIL, control plane auto-aborts (when configured), traffic split reverts to baseline, and rollout is marked aborted with correct audit trail. (3) Missing/stale metrics behavior: simulate telemetry lag and validate gate evaluation returns UNKNOWN (and is treated as fail-closed) unless an admin override is used (override actions are validated in separate unit coverage, but this suite asserts the end-to-end behavior that promotion is blocked). (4) Capacity starvation / 429 regression test: simulate small pool partitions + queue depth increase; assert routing selects baseline partition for overflow when stage partition is saturated (protects against the early beta failure mode). (5) Idempotency + concurrency: repeated promote/abort requests with the same idempotency key do not advance state twice; conflicting promotes are rejected via optimistic concurrency. (6) Rollback validation for streaming: test uses a simulated streaming request pinned to the selected partition at request start; on abort/rollback we do NOT migrate in-flight streams, but we do ensure new requests route to baseline immediately after the rollback commits. Test harness notes: These tests run in CI using the existing integration runner with a simulated Dedicated pool scheduler and in-memory telemetry backend. Gate evaluation is exercised through the policy engine path (not mocked) but telemetry queries are backed by the fake backend with deterministic timestamps to avoid flakiness. To keep runtime reasonable, we use short windows (e.g., 30s) and force sufficient sample counts. Gate thresholds in tests are intentionally low/explicit to avoid coupling to prod defaults. Files/areas changed (high level): - test/integration/dedicated_rollouts/*: new staged rollout integration suite and fixtures - test/integration/helpers/sim_dedicated_pool*: simulated pool + partitioning model (replica-based) - test/integration/helpers/fake_telemetry_backend*: deterministic metrics store + query helpers - control_plane/test_support/audit_capture*: capture + assert audit events emitted during integration runs - routing/test_support/partition_assertions*: assertions for stage partition selection and fallback behavior - ci/integration-test-manifest.yml: registers new suite, marks as required for rollouts label Notes on determinism and flake control: The suite runs with seeded randomness (SEED env) and uses monotonic time under the test clock. We also added a guard that fails the test if any telemetry series uses unbounded label sets (protects cardinality regressions). Checklist: - [x] Covers create -> promote -> complete - [x] Covers gate fail -> abort -> rollback - [x] Covers missing metrics behavior (fail-closed) - [x] Covers 429 regression scenario with fallback - [x] Validates audit events for promote/abort - [x] Validates idempotency/retry semantics - [x] CI integration job added (required for rollouts PRs) Follow-ups (not in this PR): - Expand quality regression gate coverage once eval harness integration is wired into the integration runner (Selene/Olivia). - Add multi-region impairment scenario (region down mid-stage) once routing multi-region simulator is in the test harness.
commits: test(integration): add Dedicated staged rollout e2e suite (happy path + abort/rollback)
test(harness): add simulated Dedicated pool partitions + saturation model
test(harness): add fake telemetry backend with staleness + query helpers
test(assertions): verify audit events + idempotency semantics in integration runs
ci: register dedicated-rollouts integration suite as required for rollouts changes
review_conversation: Ethan Park: The rollback test looks good, but please assert the rollout plan state machine fields (held/aborted/completed) rather than just the HTTP response. Also, can we assert the audit event includes old_stage/new_stage and idempotency key? Leila Farouk: Added explicit assertions on plan.state, plan.current_stage_index, and captured audit events. Also asserted audit payload contains old_stage, new_stage, override=false, and idempotency_key. Jordan Lee: On missing metrics test: we agreed fail-closed, but the test currently treats UNKNOWN as pass for stage 0. That’s risky. Please align with policy engine semantics: UNKNOWN should block promotion unless force-promote. Leila Farouk: Updated: UNKNOWN now blocks promotion for all non-terminal stages. Added a separate assertion that an admin-only override path exists (but not exercised end-to-end here). Mina Haddad: Re: 429 regression test—can we make it more representative of the beta incident? Specifically, simulate a small pool where canary has 1 replica and gets a burst; routing should fallback to baseline when queue depth breaches threshold. Leila Farouk: Updated the simulator to model queue depth per partition and to trip fallback once queue_depth > threshold. Test now asserts initial requests go to canary then new requests route to baseline when saturated. Rafael Mendes: Please ensure the suite is stable and won’t flap on CI. The window lengths and sample counts need to be deterministic. Also, mark the suite required only for rollouts-related changes to avoid slowing unrelated PRs. Leila Farouk: Added test clock + seeded RNG; removed reliance on wall clock. CI manifest now scopes the required suite behind labels/path filters (dedicated/rollouts/control_plane/routing). Connor O’Brien: Looks ready. Please add a note in the CI job description on how to re-run locally and how to set SEED when debugging. Leila Farouk: Added to ci/integration-test-manifest.yml and test/README.md section for integration runner. Approved.
approvals: Approved by Connor O'Brien, Ethan Park, Jordan Lee, Mina Haddad, Rafael Mendes.
